newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL noon rubber down, INRO 5-day nearer to "may-buy".
newsitem.headline: KL noon rubber down, INRO 5-day nearer to "may-buy".

text.p: Rubber prices in Malaysia were lower at midday, extending overnight losses due to a fall in Tokyo and lack of buying from consumers, dealers said.
"Again there was not much interest from the buyers side," a trader said, adding that players were not interested at current levels on expectations that prices could fall further.

"People are also concerned about the five-day moving average moving nearer to "may-buy" level," a dealer said. INRO"s may-buy level was 183.56 Malaysian/Singapore cents a kg on July 9 against 185.11 cents on July 8.
Dealers expect some enquiries from far-east buyers particularly from the South Korea and China.
Other grades like SMR CV was quoted sellers at 300 cents, MR L at 281, SMR 10 at 234 and latex at 198 cents.
At midday close, the August Int. Ones RSS buyer slipped 1.50 cents to 228 cents and August SMR 20 buyer down half a cent at 232.50 cents.
Malaysia-based shipping brokers quoted freight rates for rubber from Malaysia to Rotterdam at $700 per 20-ft container, and $1,400 per 40-ft container.
